findings.message: ensureDataKey writes to secrets.data_key through a raw withTenant transaction, outside defineService. That breaks the architecture.md law that every write goes through authorize → validate → write → audit → emit. Before this change the key row was written inside the audited putSecret transaction. Now a tenant's root data key is created with no audit record and no event. The permission check exists only because the putSecret wrapper happens to call authorize first, and any other caller of ensureDataKey skips it. Fix: make key creation a keyless defineService (for example 'secrets.data_key.create') that runs in its own committed transaction. That keeps the commit-first property and puts the write back in the pipeline.
findings.scenario: A new tenant's first putSecret → a secrets.data_key row is committed → core.audit_event has no record of the key being created (and if storeVersion then fails, an unaudited key row stays behind)

findings.message: Last round's defect was the savepoint case: a data key inserted inside a subtransaction read as committed and was cached before commit. The finding asked for a test that runs putSecret under a savepoint that rolls back. The new table covers only failure points in a top-level putSecret, and the old xmin-based code already passed all four of those, so the test does not fail without the fix. Add rows where putSecret runs inside an outer transaction or SAVEPOINT (a nested tx.transaction, or a service called from another service's run) that rolls back. Then assert that a later value is still readable after the cache is reset.
findings.scenario: Restore the old xmin check in dataKeyFor → all four it.each cases stay green, so the savepoint credential-loss path is unproven

findings.message: The checker is still not fail-closed for the types it doesn't model. (1) Non-string primitives return false: a symbol carries the value in .description, and a number or bigint carries a numeric credential. (2) The Error branch runs before the PLAIN prototype check and walks only Object.values. So Error subclasses with private #fields or prototype getters pass, and so do non-enumerable own properties such as AggregateError.errors or a defineProperty'd field. That is the same non-enumerable variant fixed for plain objects through Reflect.ownKeys, now in a second copy that disagrees with the first. Fix: treat any symbol, and any number or bigint whose string form hides to something different, as a leak. For Errors, accept only the built-in Error prototypes, walk Reflect.ownKeys, and refuse subclasses. Add these to the AC-2 table.
findings.scenario: useSecret(..., async s => Symbol(s.reveal())) → assertNoLeak passes → the caller reads result.description; or async s => new AggregateError([new Error(s.reveal())], 'x') → passes

findings.message: Encoded runs are now decoded at four offsets, but a percent-encoded base64 run is still missed. ENCODED_RUN stops at '%', so encodeURIComponent(base64(...)) splits into pieces at every %2B, %2F or %3D. If the value's encoded span crosses a '+' or '/', no piece decodes to it. This is how Basic client credentials look inside a form-encoded body or query string. Fix: before matching runs, URL-decode (and base64url-normalise) the text, or add percent-decoded text as a decoding source. Add the case to the AC-2 table.
findings.scenario: fn returns `auth=${encodeURIComponent(Buffer.from(`id:${VALUE}`).toString('base64'))}` where the base64 contains '+' or '/' inside the value's span → hide() leaves it unchanged → assertNoLeak passes

findings.message: putSecret now authorizes twice: the wrapper calls authorize(ctx, MANAGE, RESOURCE, raw) on unvalidated input, then storeVersion's pipeline authorizes again on parsed input. The two checks see different inputs and can disagree. Moving key creation into its own service (see the runtime.ts finding) removes the need for the wrapper's hand-written check.
The axe scan moved from the saved page after the rotate (saved=1 banner, row Active) to the open rotate dialog. The post-save state no longer gets an a11y check. Keep both scans.

The leak walk only covers the named cases for errors and bytes. (1) The Error branch runs before the prototype check, so any Error subclass gets through even though other class instances are refused. Only name, message, stack, cause and own enumerable values are walked. Missed: prototype getters and #private fields on subclasses (for example an HttpError that keeps the response body in #body behind `get body()`), AggregateError.errors (an own non-enumerable property), and any property added with defineProperty and enumerable:false. (2) Bytes are always read as latin1. A value stored as UTF-16 (Buffer.from(v, 'utf16le'), or a Uint16Array of char codes) becomes the value interleaved with NULs, so hide() never matches it. Fix: for Errors, walk Reflect.ownKeys and refuse any Error whose prototype is not a built-in Error prototype. Read bytes as both utf8/latin1 and utf16le. Add AggregateError, a subclass with a private field or getter, and UTF-16 bytes to the AC-2 table.
findings.scenario: useSecret(ctx, req, async (s) => new AggregateError([new Error(s.reveal())])) → partsOf walks name/message/stack/cause plus Object.values (empty), never reads .errors → the result is returned with the plaintext inside

findings.message: The table does not test the variant that sank the previous fix: putSecret running under a savepoint that rolls back (a nested tx.transaction, or a service called inside another service's run). All four rows are top-level failures, and the round-2 xmin check already handled those correctly. So the table stays green with this round's fix reverted and proves nothing about it. Add a row that calls putSecret inside an outer transaction or savepoint that rolls back. Then assert that a later put and use in a fresh runtime still decrypt.
findings.scenario: Revert runtime.ts to the xmin/pg_current_xact_id_if_assigned version → all four FAILURE_POINTS rows still pass, even though putSecret under a rolled-back SAVEPOINT caches a key that was never committed
